source "https://rubygems.org"
git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

ruby "3.3.6"

# Bundle edge Rails instead: gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
gem "rails", "7.0.8.7"
gem "concurrent-ruby", "1.3.4"

# The original asset pipeline for Rails [https://github.com/rails/sprockets-rails]
gem "sprockets-rails"

# Use postgresql as the database for Active Record
gem "pg", "1.6.0"

# Use the Puma web server [https://github.com/puma/puma]
gem "puma", "~> 5.0"

# Use JavaScript with ESM import maps [https://github.com/rails/importmap-rails]
gem "importmap-rails"

# Hotwire's SPA-like page accelerator [https://turbo.hotwired.dev]
gem "turbo-rails"

# Hotwire's modest JavaScript framework [https://stimulus.hotwired.dev]
gem "stimulus-rails"

# Build JSON APIs with ease [https://github.com/rails/jbuilder]
gem "jbuilder"

# Paginate the note list [https://github.com/ddnexus/pagy]
gem "pagy", "8.6.3"

# Run Active Job on Redis through Sidekiq [https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq]
gem "sidekiq", "6.5.12"
gem "redis", "4.8.1"

# Request citation metadata over HTTP [https://github.com/lostisland/faraday]
gem "faraday", "1.10.4"

# Use Kredis to get higher-level data types in Redis [https://github.com/rails/kredis]
# gem "kredis"

# Use Active Model has_secure_password [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_model_basics.html#securepassword]
gem "bcrypt", "~> 3.1.7"

# Windows does not include zoneinfo files, so bundle the tzinfo-data gem
gem "tzinfo-data", platforms: %i[ mingw mswin x64_mingw jruby ]

# Reduces boot times through caching; required in config/boot.rb
gem "bootsnap", require: false

# Use Sass to process CSS
# gem "sassc-rails"

# Use Active Storage variants [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#transforming-images]
# gem "image_processing", "~> 1.2"

group :development, :test do
  # See https://guides.rubyonrails.org/debugging_rails_applications.html#debugging-with-the-debug-gem
  gem "debug", platforms: %i[ mri mingw x64_mingw ]
end

group :development do
  # Use console on exceptions pages [https://github.com/rails/web-console]
  gem "web-console"

  # Add speed badges [https://github.com/MiniProfiler/rack-mini-profiler]
  # gem "rack-mini-profiler"

  # Speed up commands on slow machines / big apps [https://github.com/rails/spring]
  # gem "spring"
end

group :test do
  # Use system testing [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/testing.html#system-testing]
  gem "capybara"
  gem "selenium-webdriver"

  # Rails 7.0's test runner is incompatible with Minitest 6
  gem "minitest", "~> 5.25"
end

content.content:
# Architecture

## Starting point

Margin Notes is a reading-notebook application. Implemented so far:

- A reader (`User`) signs in with email and password through `has_secure_password`.
  `SessionsController` stores only the user ID in the Rails session.
  `ApplicationController#require_sign_in` protects the application's other
  controllers, but not Rails' Active Storage controllers.
- A reader owns `Notebook`s, and each `Note` belongs to one notebook. A note's
  owner is its notebook's owner, so `User#notes` (through notebooks) is the
  authorized note scope. There is no separate `user_id` on notes.
- `NotesController#index` serves `/notes` and its `/journal` alias. It lists the
  reader's notes newest first with an ID tie-breaker, and supports title search
  and notebook and status filters. `show` renders one note's rich body.
- Pagy 8.6.3 paginates that filtered list after ordering, 10 notes per page by
  default. The search form offers 5, 10, 25, or 50 as the `per_page` URL
  parameter. Larger requested sizes are capped at 50. Next and previous links keep
  the filters and page size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric page shows the
  first page, and a page past the end shows the last page. The form never sends
  an invalid size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric `per_page` in a URL is
  not handled, and Pagy raises `Pagy::VariableError`.
- A note's body is Action Text (`has_rich_text :body`), edited with Trix.
  Attachments are Active Storage blobs on the local Disk service. `Note` rejects
  saves that embed a blob over 1 MB. Direct uploads store blobs before this
  validation, without a size limit. Rejected or abandoned uploads remain
  unattached, and nothing purges them. No image processor is installed, so images
  use the original blobs, not variants. A migration converted existing plain-text
  bodies to escaped rich text.
- Action Text sanitizes rich text when it renders. The
  [Action Text initializer](config/initializers/action_text.rb) adds
  `details`/`summary` to the default allowlist for collapsible excerpts. Trix
  does not support those elements. Stored excerpts render as collapsible content,
  but saving them through the editor permanently flattens that structure, even
  when only tags or highlight change.
- Note tags are a JSON array in a text column, entered as a comma-separated
  list (`Note#tag_list`). The highlight color is `color` in the `settings` jsonb
  column, which the form edits as `highlight_color`.
- `NotebooksController#edit`/`update` are notebook settings. The slug is derived
  from the name on creation and is read-only afterward (`attr_readonly`). The
  settings form resubmits it unchanged. The export heading is stored in the
  serialized `preferences` hash. Markdown exports use both.
- A reader imports a CSV into one owned notebook. `ImportPreviewsController`
  reads the upload and renders a preview without saving. The preview page sends
  the CSV text back in a hidden field, and `ImportsController#create` reads and
  validates it again rather than trusting the preview. `Import#apply` saves the
  import and each row's note in one transaction. If any row cannot be saved,
  nothing from the batch remains. The receipt page and its CSV download list
  each imported note's title and DOI. Submitting the same preview twice creates
  two imports.
- `Import` accepts one format: UTF-8 CSV with the header row
  `title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch`, at most 100 notes and 100 KB.
  Only the title is required. Previews identify rows by their source line, so a
  quoted multi-line body keeps the line where its row starts. Body HTML takes the
  same Action Text assignment and render-time sanitization as the editor.
- A `Citation` is identified by its DOI, the table's `doi` primary key, and is
  shared by every reader who cites it. A DOI is stored as given apart from
  surrounding whitespace, so case variants are different citations. Rows in one
  import share a new citation. Two simultaneous imports that introduce the same
  new DOI can conflict; the losing request fails with a server error and saves
  nothing. A reader's annotation and optional reminder epoch belong to the note,
  not the citation. Annotations are plain text in both the preview and note page;
  line breaks are preserved on the note page, but markup is displayed literally.
  Applying an import does not schedule its reminders; the reader schedules each
  one from its note.
- A reader can also enter a DOI on the note form (`Note#doi=`), which cites the
  shared citation with that exact, trimmed DOI or creates it.
- A reader requests metadata for the citation on one of their notes with
  `CitationEnrichmentsController#create`, nested under the note. It resolves the
  note through `current_user.notes`, so another reader's note, or a note without
  a DOI, is a 404. `Citation#request_enrichment` marks the citation pending and
  queues `CitationEnrichmentJob`, unless a request is already pending. The job
  calls `Citation#enrich`, which stores the provider's title and source URL and
  marks the citation completed, or records a failure message. Metadata and
  status belong to the shared citation, so every note citing the DOI shows them.
  The note page shows the state; it does not update itself while pending.
- `Citation::Provider` is the HTTP client for the metadata provider. It reads
  its URL and basic-auth credentials from [config/secrets.yml](config/secrets.yml)
  through `Rails.application.secrets`; that file reads them from the environment.
  Faraday retries a GET once on 503. A 401, 403, or 404, or a response without a
  title and an http(s) URL, fails the enrichment at once. A 429 or 5xx, timeout,
  or connection failure raises `Citation::Provider::Unavailable`. The job retries
  that with `retry_on`, three attempts in all at exponentially longer waits, then
  records the failure instead of passing the error to Sidekiq's own retries. A
  persistently unavailable provider therefore receives at most six requests per
  enrichment request. A job that fails for another reason uses Sidekiq's retries
  and leaves the citation pending meanwhile.
- [bin/citation-provider](bin/citation-provider) is a deterministic local stand-in
  for the provider, used for development and demonstrations. No real provider or
  credentials are configured.
- A reader exports an owned notebook as Markdown from its exports page
  (`ExportsController`, nested under the notebook). `Notebook#request_export`
  saves a queued `Export`, then queues the native Sidekiq job `ExportJob` and
  stores its job ID, which the page shows. The export is committed before the
  job is queued so the worker can always load it. If Redis refuses the job, the
  export is removed and the request fails. Each request creates a new export.
- `Export#generate`, run by the worker, marks the export working with the
  notebook's note count, then writes the notes oldest first (creation time, then
  ID). The file starts with the notebook's export heading, or its name when none
  is set. Each note is a second-level heading with its title on one line,
  followed by its body as Action Text plain text. Markdown characters are not
  escaped. Progress is saved after each note. A retried job starts again from
  the first note. There is no failed state: while Sidekiq retries a failing job,
  the export shows as working and the reader can cancel it.
- Cancelling (`ExportCancellationsController`) sets a queued or working export's
  persisted status to cancelled under its row lock. The worker checks that status
  before each note and before completing, then stops and keeps no file. Completed
  and cancelled exports cannot be cancelled.
- The worker uploads the file to Active Storage (`<slug>.md`) before marking the
  export completed, so a completed export always has a file. It can be downloaded
  for 24 hours (`Export::AVAILABLE_FOR`). `ExportDownloadsController` resolves the
  export through the reader's notebook, so another reader's export is a 404, and
  checks `Export#downloadable?` on every request before any conditional response.
  An expired, cancelled, or unfinished export redirects to the exports page. The
  file is sent by the application, never by an Active Storage URL, with an ETag
  and Last-Modified from the stored file and `private, must-revalidate`.
  A failed upload can leave an unattached blob row without a stored file. Nothing
  cleans up those rows, and each failed retry can leave another one.
- The exports page caches each completed export's availability indicator as a
  fragment that expires at the export's deadline. The download action does not
  read that cache. The page does not update itself while an export is queued or
  working. Nothing purges expired files; they remain in storage.
- A notebook's activity page (`ActivityReportsController#show`, nested under the
  notebook and linked from the notebooks list) shows how many of its notes were
  created on each UTC date, newest date first. It is read-only and resolves the
  notebook through `current_user.notebooks`, so another reader's notebook is a
  404. `Notebook#daily_note_counts` groups the notes by `DATE(created_at)` in
  PostgreSQL and reads the rows with a raw `select_rows`, which returns each date
  as ISO 8601 text; the method parses it with `Date.iso8601`. Every status counts,
  and dates without notes are omitted. The report is derived from the notes that
  exist when it is requested, not an activity log: deleting a note lowers its
  date's count, and nothing records past counts.
- Each reader has a time zone (`User#time_zone`, UTC by default), chosen on the
  account settings page (`AccountsController`). Reminder times use it. Digests
  follow UTC days, and other pages still show times in UTC.
- A note's reminder is its `reminder_epoch`, a time in seconds since 1970, set by
  an import or by the reader. `RemindersController#create`, nested under the
  note, reads a date and time the reader entered in their time zone
  (`User#local_time`), or, with none, uses the stored time. `Note#schedule_reminder`
  queues `NoteReminderJob` for that time with `set(wait_until:)` and stores the
  job's ID, under the note's row lock, so a failed enqueue keeps the earlier
  reminder. A local time that does not exist because of a daylight saving change
  moves forward, and an ambiguous one takes its first occurrence. A time in the
  past is sent as soon as a worker runs the job.
- Scheduling again, or postponing (`ReminderPostponementsController`), replaces the
  reminder. Earlier jobs stay in Sidekiq's schedule, but send nothing: when a job
  runs, `Note#send_reminder` takes the row lock and emails the reader only if its
  job ID is still the note's and the reminder has not been sent, then records
  `reminder_sent_at`. The note page shows whether a reminder is imported but not
  scheduled, scheduled, or sent. A job that fails after the email is written can
  send it again when Sidekiq retries it.
- Postponing moves the reminder 24 elapsed hours later. The note page previews
  that time as `reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`, which keeps the reminder's UTC
  offset. Across a daylight saving change the preview shows the right instant,
  but at a different offset and wall-clock time from the postponed reminder.
- A reader requests a digest of their ready notes from the notes page
  (`DigestsController`). `User#request_digest` reserves the reader's ID in a
  Redis set for the request's UTC date
  (`digest_requests:YYYY-MM-DD`, kept for two days) and queues `DigestJob` with
  the reader, the request time in the reader's zone, and the share of their notes
  that are ready, as a `BigDecimal`. A reader whose ID is already in the day's set
  is told the digest was already requested. If the job cannot be queued, the
  reservation is removed and the error raised, so the request fails and can be
  repeated. The reservation prevents repeated requests, not repeated emails:
  Sidekiq can run a job more than once. Each request logs redis-rb's deprecation
  warning for a single-member `sadd`, and Sidekiq warns that the job's arguments
  are not native JSON types, because of the `BigDecimal`.
- Sidekiq stores the job's arguments as JSON. Active Job 7.0 sends the request
  time with its UTC offset but deserializes it in the worker's zone, UTC, and the
  completion arrives as a decimal string such as `"0.6667"`. `DigestMailer` lists
  the reader's ready notes last updated during that UTC day, and dates the digest
  by it. The content day matches the reservation's day, even near local midnight.
  A digest is a snapshot when its job runs; notes updated afterward are not sent
  in a second digest for that UTC day.
- The mailers write plain-text email. Development writes each recipient's email
  to `tmp/mails` (Action Mailer's file delivery); tests use the `:test` delivery
  method. Production has no delivery method or link host configured.
- Active Storage serves blobs through signed URLs from its own controllers. Those
  URLs are not checked against the signed-in reader. The embedded blob redirect
  URLs do not expire, although the Disk-service URLs they redirect to do.
  The direct-upload controller checks CSRF, not sign-in; the public sign-in page
  supplies a CSRF token to anonymous clients. This sample has no private-file
  access policy or upload-abuse protection for a public deployment.

These conventions guide further features without prescribing a schema in advance.

The initial runtime is Ruby 3.3.6 and Rails 7.0.8.7 with Rails 7.0 defaults.
[Gemfile](Gemfile), [Gemfile.lock](Gemfile.lock), [.ruby-version](.ruby-version), and
[config/application.rb](config/application.rb) are the executable sources of truth.

- PostgreSQL is the application database. Use Active Record and migrations for
  application-owned records, constraints, indexes, and transactions.
- ERB renders HTML. The generated app includes Sprockets, importmap, Turbo, and
  Stimulus. Jbuilder is available for requested JSON representations, but an HTML
  feature does not automatically need a JSON API.
- Rails includes the mailer, job, storage, and cable frameworks. Their presence
  does not mean broadcasts are implemented features. Email is sent only for
  reminders and digests, and is not delivered outside development's files. File
  uploads exist only as rich-text attachments.
- Active Job uses Sidekiq 6.5 as its adapter outside tests, so queued jobs are
  kept in Redis (`REDIS_URL`, by default `redis://localhost:6379`) and run in a
  separate `bundle exec sidekiq` process. Tests use Active Job's test adapter.
  `ExportJob` is a native Sidekiq job rather than an Active Job, so its job ID can
  be shown. Sidekiq stores its arguments as JSON, and it uses Sidekiq's default
  retries.
- Action Text 7.0.8.7 bundles Trix 1.3.4. That version cannot load saved HTML
  that has attributes, such as links or attachments, so the layout loads Trix
  1.3.5 from `vendor/javascript` as a classic script. Trix 1.x is not an ES
  module, so it is not in the import map. `@rails/actiontext` is.
  The vendored build comes from the [Trix 1.3.5 release](https://github.com/basecamp/trix/tree/1.3.5)
  and includes its [MIT license](vendor/javascript/trix-1.3.5.LICENSE).
- Orb setup starts PostgreSQL and Redis. Redis holds Sidekiq's queues and the
  digest reservations; it is not an application cache. The generated production
  cable configuration names Redis. That configuration is not a verified deployment.

## Prefer Rails objects with clear responsibilities

Use the framework's ordinary directories and interfaces:

| Responsibility | Home |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP verbs, paths, and resource nesting | `config/routes.rb` |
| Parameter selection, authorized lookup, response negotiation | `app/controllers/` |
| Persistent state and domain operations | `app/models/` |
| A cohesive capability of one model | A namespace beneath `app/models/` |
| Behavior genuinely shared across models | `app/models/concerns/` |
| HTML, Turbo stream, and JSON representations | `app/views/` |
| Presentation helpers | `app/helpers/` |
| Browser interaction around rendered HTML | `app/javascript/controllers/` |
| Background execution and retry boundary | `app/jobs/` |
| Mail composition | `app/mailers/` and its views |

A controller can call Active Record directly for a simple save. A multi-step
domain transition belongs behind a meaningful model method, not a sequence of
unrelated updates in the controller. Use a plain Ruby object or Active Model when
an operation needs its own object but no database table. Do not introduce a
mandatory service, repository, presenter, or command layer between every pair of
Rails objects.

Fizzy models closing a card as a singular closure resource. Its controller calls
`Card#close`, and `Card::Closeable` owns the association, predicates, and transaction.
The [closure sources](docs/references/fizzy.md#card-closure) illustrate a resource
boundary and a domain method, not a requirement to add cards to Margin Notes.

## Model resources, not collections of verbs

Use the conventional REST actions, including `new` and `edit` for HTML forms.
When a new operation does not fit an existing resource, look for the resource it
creates, updates, or removes before adding a custom action. Keep nesting shallow
enough that the parent conveys ownership rather than reproducing the whole schema.

Use route helpers in views and responses. Controllers choose the representation.
Models do not construct controller responses or reach into request parameters.

## Keep data ownership and effects explicit

- PostgreSQL owns durable application facts. Derive a value from those facts
  unless storing it solves a demonstrated query, history, or concurrency need.
- Put invariants used outside HTTP in the domain model. Add database constraints
  when integrity must also hold across concurrent requests and non-model writes.
- Keep related database writes in one transaction. Do not assume it can undo a
  remote request, an email, or a job already sent to another system.
- Jobs should delegate to domain behavior and carry the identifiers or context
  they need. Decide retries, duplicate delivery, and transaction timing when a
  real background feature is introduced, rather than adding a queue preemptively.
- Keep network clients at visible boundaries. Preserve failure information and
  distinguish a legitimate empty response from a failed operation.

Fizzy's [comment example](docs/references/fizzy.md#comments) enforces comment
eligibility in both the model and the controller. Callers outside HTTP must obey
the same rule.

## Authorization is not presentation

Define ownership and the authorized lookup scope together. Resolve records
through the signed-in reader: `current_user.notebooks` and `current_user.notes`.
Direct lookups outside that scope raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, which is
a 404 in production. A submitted `notebook_id` is resolved through
`current_user.notebooks.find_by`, never assigned directly. A missing or foreign
notebook fails validation and renders the form with 422, without saving the note.
Resolve nested records through their authorized parent. Neither an unguessable ID
nor a hidden or disabled button grants or checks permission.

Keep actor-dependent decisions explicit in domain APIs and reusable rendering.
If request-local state is introduced, set and reset it at the request boundary.
Jobs, mailers, and tests must not rely on a previous request having populated it.
Do not adopt a tenancy or identity scheme solely because a reference application
uses one.

## Render on the server, enhance in the browser

Use HTML forms and links for their native semantics. Turbo handles navigation,
frames, and targeted replacements. Stimulus supplies local interaction that HTML
does not provide. Keep persistence and authorization on the server, not in a
second client-side model of the domain.

Partials take the resources and presentation inputs they need. A template may
compose several resources. A reusable partial should not depend on a particular
controller's incidental instance variables or on undeclared request context.
See the [view guide](docs/guides/views.md) for HTML, accessibility, Turbo, and JSON.

## Optimize the actual representation

Start with correct queries and clear response contracts. Filter and order before
pagination. Use a stable tie-breaker where page membership must be deterministic.
Load the associations that the rendered representation uses rather than adding
a universal preload list to every request.

Define cache keys and invalidation rules before introducing caching. Include
permissions, locale, and related-record changes when they affect the output, or
keep those parts outside the shared fragment. The
[board example](docs/references/fizzy.md#boards-and-caching) illustrates why a
warm cache must be tested with another viewer, not just the same request twice.

## Scope and reference boundaries

The [public examples](docs/references/fizzy.md) are evidence for design ideas, not
a compatible application template. Their Ruby, Rails, database adapters, asset
pipeline, editors, and helper libraries differ from this repository. Use the
locked local APIs, and introduce new infrastructure only for a requested feature.

As features land, document their ownership and invariants here. Keep detailed
layer practices in the [model](docs/guides/models.md),
[controller](docs/guides/controllers.md), and [view](docs/guides/views.md) guides,
and verification rules in [TESTING.md](TESTING.md).

# frozen_string_literal: true

gem "sidekiq", ">= 4.1.0"
require "sidekiq"

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # = Sidekiq adapter for Active Job
    #
    # Simple, efficient background processing for Ruby. Sidekiq uses threads to
    # handle many jobs at the same time in the same process. It does not
    # require \Rails but will integrate tightly with it to make background
    # processing dead simple.
    #
    # Read more about Sidekiq {here}[http://sidekiq.org].
    #
    # To use Sidekiq set the queue_adapter config to +:sidekiq+.
    #
    #   Rails.application.config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq
    class SidekiqAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      def initialize(*) # :nodoc:
        @stopping = false

        Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end

        Sidekiq.configure_client do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end
      end

      def check_adapter
        ActiveJob.deprecator.warn <<~MSG.squish
          The built-in `sidekiq` adapter is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 8.2.
          Please upgrade `sidekiq` gem to version 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.
        MSG
      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name
        ).perform_async(job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name,
        ).perform_at(timestamp, job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_all(jobs) # :nodoc:
        enqueued_count = 0
        jobs.group_by(&:class).each do |job_class, same_class_jobs|
          same_class_jobs.group_by(&:queue_name).each do |queue, same_class_and_queue_jobs|
            immediate_jobs, scheduled_jobs = same_class_and_queue_jobs.partition { |job| job.scheduled_at.nil? }

            if immediate_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => immediate_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end

            if scheduled_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
                "at" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| job.scheduled_at&.to_f }
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end
          end
        end
        enqueued_count
      end

      class JobWrapper # :nodoc:
        include Sidekiq::Worker

        def perform(job_data)
          Base.execute job_data.merge("provider_job_id" => jid)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

    Deserializes `enqueued_at` as a Time instead of ISO8601 String.

## Rails 7.1.0.beta1 (September 13, 2023) ##
*   Fix Active Job log message to correctly report a job failed to enqueue
    when the adapter raises an `ActiveJob::EnqueueError`.
    *Ben Sheldon*
*   Add `after_discard` method.
    This method lets job authors define a block which will be run when a job is about to be discarded. For example:
    ```ruby
    class AfterDiscardJob < ActiveJob::Base
      after_discard do |job, exception|
        Rails.logger.info("#{job.class} raised an exception: #{exception}")
      end
      def perform
        raise StandardError
      end
    end
    ```
    The above job will run the block passed to `after_discard` after the job is discarded. The exception will
    still be raised after the block has been run.
    *Rob Cardy*
*   Fix deserialization of ActiveSupport::Duration
    Previously, a deserialized Duration would return an array from Duration#parts.
    It will now return a hash just like a regular Duration.
    This also fixes an error when trying to add or subtract from a deserialized Duration
    (eg `duration + 1.year`).
    *Jonathan del Strother*
*   `perform_enqueued_jobs` is now compatible with all Active Job adapters
    This means that methods that depend on it, like Action Mailer's `assert_emails`,
    will work correctly even if the test adapter is not used.
    *Alex Ghiculescu*
*   Allow queue adapters to provide a custom name by implementing `queue_adapter_name`
    *Sander Verdonschot*
*   Log background job enqueue callers
    Add `verbose_enqueue_logs` configuration option to display the caller
    of background job enqueue in the log to help with debugging.
    Example log line:
    ```
    Enqueued AvatarThumbnailsJob (Job ID: ab528951-41fb-4c48-9129-3171791c27d6) to Sidekiq(default) with arguments: 1092412064
    ↳ app/models/user.rb:421:in `generate_avatar_thumbnails'
    ```
    Enabled in development only for new and upgraded applications. Not recommended for use
    in the production environment since it relies on Ruby's `Kernel#caller` which is fairly slow.
    *fatkodima*
*   Set `provider_job_id` for Backburner jobs
    *Cameron Matheson*
*   Add `perform_all_later` to enqueue multiple jobs at once
    This adds the ability to bulk enqueue jobs, without running callbacks, by
    passing multiple jobs or an array of jobs. For example:
    ```ruby
    ActiveJob.perform_all_later(MyJob.new("hello", 42), MyJob.new("world", 0))
    user_jobs = User.pluck(:id).map { |id| UserJob.new(user_id: id) }
    ActiveJob.perform_all_later(user_jobs)
    ```
    This can greatly reduce the number of round-trips to the queue datastore.
    For queue adapters that do not implement the new `enqueue_all` method, we
    fall back to enqueuing jobs individually. The Sidekiq adapter implements
    `enqueue_all` with `push_bulk`.
    This method does not use the existing `enqueue.active_job` event, but adds a
    new event `enqueue_all.active_job`.
    *Sander Verdonschot*
*   Don't double log the `job` when using `ActiveRecord::QueryLog`

content.content:
*   Don't double log the `job` when using `ActiveRecord::QueryLog`
    Previously if you set `config.active_record.query_log_tags` to an array that included
    `:job`, the job name would get logged twice. This bug has been fixed.
    *Alex Ghiculescu*
*   Add support for Sidekiq's transaction-aware client
    *Jonathan del Strother*
*   Remove QueAdapter from Active Job.
    After maintaining Active Job QueAdapter by Rails and Que side
    to support Ruby 3 keyword arguments and options provided as top level keywords,
    it is quite difficult to maintain it this way.
    Active Job Que adapter can be included in the future version of que gem itself.
    *Yasuo Honda*
*   Fix BigDecimal (de)serialization for adapters using JSON.
    Previously, BigDecimal was listed as not needing a serializer.  However,
    when used with an adapter storing the job arguments as JSON, it would get
    serialized as a simple String, resulting in deserialization also producing
    a String (instead of a BigDecimal).
    By using a serializer, we ensure the round trip is safe.
    To ensure applications using BigDecimal job arguments are not subject to
    race conditions during deployment (where a replica running a version of
    Rails without BigDecimalSerializer fails to deserialize an argument
    serialized with it), `ActiveJob.use_big_decimal_serializer` is disabled by
    default, and can be set to true in a following deployment..
    *Sam Bostock*
*   Preserve full-precision `enqueued_at` timestamps for serialized jobs,
    allowing more accurate reporting of how long a job spent waiting in the
    queue before it was performed.
    Retains IS08601 format compatibility.
    *Jeremy Daer*
*   Add `--parent` option to job generator to specify parent class of job.
    Example:
    `bin/rails g job process_payment --parent=payment_job` generates:
    ```ruby
    class ProcessPaymentJob < PaymentJob
      # ...
    end
    ```
    *Gannon McGibbon*
*   Add more detailed description to job generator.
    *Gannon McGibbon*
*   `perform.active_job` notification payloads now include `:db_runtime`, which
    is the total time (in ms) taken by database queries while performing a job.
    This value can be used to better understand how a job's time is spent.
    *Jonathan Hefner*
*   Update `ActiveJob::QueueAdapters::QueAdapter` to remove deprecation warning.
    Remove a deprecation warning introduced in que 1.2 to prepare for changes in
    que 2.0 necessary for Ruby 3 compatibility.
    *Damir Zekic* and *Adis Hasovic*
*   Add missing `bigdecimal` require in `ActiveJob::Arguments`
    Could cause `uninitialized constant ActiveJob::Arguments::BigDecimal (NameError)`
    when loading Active Job in isolation.
    *Jean Boussier*
*   Allow testing `discard_on/retry_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError`
    Previously in `perform_enqueued_jobs`, `deserialize_arguments_if_needed`
    was called before calling `perform_now`. When a record no longer exists
    and is serialized using GlobalID this led to raising
    an `ActiveJob::DeserializationError` before reaching `perform_now` call.
    This behavior makes difficult testing the job `discard_on/retry_on` logic.
    Now `deserialize_arguments_if_needed` call is postponed to when `perform_now`
    is called.
    Example:
    ```ruby
    class UpdateUserJob < ActiveJob::Base
      discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError
      def perform(user)
        # ...
      end
    end
    # In the test
    User.destroy_all
    assert_nothing_raised do
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: UpdateUserJob
    end
    ```
    *Jacopo Beschi*

## Rails 7.2.0 (August 09, 2024) ##
*   All tests now respect the `active_job.queue_adapter` config.
    Previously if you had set `config.active_job.queue_adapter` in your `config/application.rb`
    or `config/environments/test.rb` file, the adapter you selected was previously not used consistently
    across all tests. In some tests your adapter would be used, but other tests would use the `TestAdapter`.
    In Rails 7.2, all tests will respect the `queue_adapter` config if provided. If no config is provided,
    the `TestAdapter` will continue to be used.
    See [#48585](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/48585) for more details.
    *Alex Ghiculescu*
*   Make Active Job transaction aware when used conjointly with Active Record.
    A common mistake with Active Job is to enqueue jobs from inside a transaction,
    causing them to potentially be picked and ran by another process, before the
    transaction is committed, which may result in various errors.
    ```ruby
    Topic.transaction do
      topic = Topic.create(...)
      NewTopicNotificationJob.perform_later(topic)
    end
    ```
    Now Active Job will automatically defer the enqueuing to after the transaction is committed,
    and drop the job if the transaction is rolled back.
    Various queue implementations can choose to disable this behavior, and users can disable it,
    or force it on a per job basis:
    ```ruby
    class NewTopicNotificationJob < ApplicationJob
      self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = :never # or `:always` or `:default`
    end
    ```
    *Jean Boussier*, *Cristian Bica*
*   Do not trigger immediate loading of `ActiveJob::Base` when loading `ActiveJob::TestHelper`.
    *Maxime Réty*
*   Preserve the serialized timezone when deserializing `ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone` arguments.
    *Joshua Young*
*   Remove deprecated `:exponentially_longer` value for the `:wait` in `retry_on`.
    *Rafael Mendonça França*
*   Remove deprecated support to set numeric values to `scheduled_at` attribute.
    *Rafael Mendonça França*
*   Deprecate `Rails.application.config.active_job.use_big_decimal_serialize`.
    *Rafael Mendonça França*
*   Remove deprecated primitive serializer for `BigDecimal` arguments.
    *Rafael Mendonça França*

## Rails 8.1.0 (October 22, 2025) ##
*   Add structured events for Active Job:
    - `active_job.enqueued`
    - `active_job.bulk_enqueued`
    - `active_job.started`
    - `active_job.completed`
    - `active_job.retry_scheduled`
    - `active_job.retry_stopped`
    - `active_job.discarded`
    - `active_job.interrupt`
    - `active_job.resume`
    - `active_job.step_skipped`
    - `active_job.step_started`
    - `active_job.step`
    *Adrianna Chang*
*   Deprecate built-in `sidekiq` adapter.
    If you're using this adapter, upgrade to `sidekiq` 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.
    *fatkodima*
*   Remove deprecated internal `SuckerPunch` adapter in favor of the adapter included with the `sucker_punch` gem.
    *Rafael Mendonça França*
*   Remove support to set `ActiveJob::Base.enqueue_after_transaction_commit` to `:never`, `:always` and `:default`.
    *Rafael Mendonça França*
*   Remove deprecated `Rails.application.config.active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit`.
    *Rafael Mendonça França*
*   `ActiveJob::Serializers::ObjectSerializers#klass` method is now public.
    Custom Active Job serializers must have a public `#klass` method too.
    The returned class will be index allowing for faster serialization.
    *Jean Boussier*
*   Allow jobs to the interrupted and resumed with Continuations
    A job can use Continuations by including the `ActiveJob::Continuable`
    concern. Continuations split jobs into steps. When the queuing system
    is shutting down jobs can be interrupted and their progress saved.
    ```ruby
    class ProcessImportJob
      include ActiveJob::Continuable
      def perform(import_id)
        @import = Import.find(import_id)
        # block format
        step :initialize do
          @import.initialize
        end
        # step with cursor, the cursor is saved when the job is interrupted
        step :process do |step|
          @import.records.find_each(start: step.cursor) do |record|
            record.process
            step.advance! from: record.id
          end
        end
        # method format
        step :finalize
        private
          def finalize
            @import.finalize
          end
      end
    end
    ```
    *Donal McBreen*
*   Defer invocation of ActiveJob enqueue callbacks until after commit when
    `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` is enabled.
    *Will Roever*
*   Add `report:` option to `ActiveJob::Base#retry_on` and `#discard_on`
    When the `report:` option is passed, errors will be reported to the error reporter
    before being retried / discarded.
    *Andrew Novoselac*
*   Accept a block for `ActiveJob::ConfiguredJob#perform_later`.
    This was inconsistent with a regular `ActiveJob::Base#perform_later`.
    *fatkodima*
*   Raise a more specific error during deserialization when a previously serialized job class is now unknown.
    `ActiveJob::UnknownJobClassError` will be raised instead of a more generic
    `NameError` to make it easily possible for adapters to tell if the `NameError`
    was raised during job execution or deserialization.
    *Earlopain*

module ActiveJob
  module EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit # :nodoc:
    private
      def raw_enqueue
        if self.class.enqueue_after_transaction_commit
          self.successfully_enqueued = true
          ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
            self.successfully_enqueued = false
            super
          end
          self
        else
          super
        end
      end
  end

    *Petrik de Heus*

*   Bring back the historical behavior of committing transaction on non-local return.

    ```ruby
    Model.transaction do
      model.save
      return
      other_model.save # not executed
    end
    ```

    Historically only raised errors would trigger a rollback, but in Ruby `2.3`, the `timeout` library
    started using `throw` to interrupt execution which had the adverse effect of committing open transactions.

    To solve this, in Active Record 6.1 the behavior was changed to instead rollback the transaction as it was safer
    than to potentially commit an incomplete transaction.

    Using `return`, `break` or `throw` inside a `transaction` block was essentially deprecated from Rails 6.1 onwards.

    However with the release of `timeout 0.4.0`, `Timeout.timeout` now raises an error again, and Active Record is able
    to return to its original, less surprising, behavior.

    This historical behavior can now be opt-ed in via:

    ```
    Rails.application.config.active_record.commit_transaction_on_non_local_return = true
    ```

    And is the default for new applications created in Rails 7.1.

## Rails 7.1.0.beta1 (September 13, 2023) ## * Use `Rails::HTML5::SafeListSanitizer` by default in the Rails 7.1 configuration if it is supported. Action Text's sanitizer can be configured by setting `config.action_text.sanitizer_vendor`. Supported values are `Rails::HTML4::Sanitizer` or `Rails::HTML5::Sanitizer`. The Rails 7.1 configuration will set this to `Rails::HTML5::Sanitizer` when it is supported, and fall back to `Rails::HTML4::Sanitizer`. Previous configurations default to `Rails::HTML4::Sanitizer`. As a result of this change, the defaults for `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags` and `.allowed_attributes` are applied at runtime, so the value of these attributes is now 'nil' unless set by the application. You may call `sanitizer_allowed_tags` or `sanitizer_allowed_attributes` to inspect the tags and attributes being allowed by the sanitizer. *Mike Dalessio* * Attachables now can override default attachment missing template. require "action_text/system_test_helper" include ActionText::SystemTestHelper end end initializer "action_text.configure" do |app| ActionText::Attachment.tag_name = app.config.action_text.attachment_tag_name end config.after_initialize do |app| if klass = app.config.action_text.sanitizer_vendor ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_view) do ActionText::ContentHelper.sanitizer = klass.safe_list_sanitizer.new end end end end end ## Rails 8.1.0 (October 22, 2025) ## * De-couple `@rails/actiontext/attachment_upload.js` from `Trix.Attachment` Implement `@rails/actiontext/index.js` with a `direct-upload:progress` event listeners and `Promise` resolution. *Sean Doyle* * Capture block content for form helper methods ```erb <%= rich_textarea_tag :content, nil do %>

hello world

<% end %> <%= rich_textarea :message, :content, input: "trix_input_1" do %>

hello world

<% end %> <%= form_with model: Message.new do |form| %> <%= form.rich_textarea :content do %>

hello world

<% end %> <% end %> ``` *Sean Doyle* * Generalize `:rich_text_area` Capybara selector Prepare for more Action Text-capable WYSIWYG editors by making `:rich_text_area` rely on the presence of `[role="textbox"]` and `[contenteditable]` HTML attributes rather than a `` element. *Sean Doyle* * Forward `fill_in_rich_text_area` options to Capybara ```ruby fill_in_rich_textarea "Rich text editor", id: "trix_editor_1", with: "Hello world!" ``` *Sean Doyle* * Attachment upload progress accounts for server processing time. *Jeremy Daer* * The Trix dependency is now satisfied by a gem, `action_text-trix`, rather than vendored files. This allows applications to bump Trix versions independently of Rails releases. Effectively this also upgrades Trix to `>= 2.1.15`. *Mike Dalessio* * Change `ActionText::RichText#embeds` assignment from `before_save` to `before_validation` *Sean Doyle* Please check [8-0-stable](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8-0-stable/actiontext/CHANGELOG.md) for previous changes.

## Rails 8.1.0 (October 22, 2025) ##

*   Remove deprecated passing a Time object to `Time#since`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated `Benchmark.ms` method. It is now defined in the `benchmark` gem.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated addition for `Time` instances with `ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated support for `to_time` to preserve the system local time. It will now always preserve the receiver
    timezone.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Deprecate `config.active_support.to_time_preserves_timezone`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Standardize event name formatting in `assert_event_reported` error messages.

    The event name in failure messages now uses `.inspect` (e.g., `name: "user.created"`)
    to match `assert_events_reported` and provide type clarity between strings and symbols.
    This only affects tests that assert on the failure message format itself.

    *George Ma*
    *Igor Depolli*

*   Improve error message when using `assert_difference` or `assert_changes` with a
    proc by printing the proc's source code (MRI only).

    *Richard Böhme*, *Jean Boussier*

*   Add a new configuration value `:zone` for `ActiveSupport.to_time_preserves_timezone` and rename the previous `true` value to `:offset`. The new default value is `:zone`.

    *Jason Kim*, *John Hawthorn*

*   Align instrumentation `payload[:key]` in ActiveSupport::Cache to follow the same pattern, with namespaced and normalized keys.

    *Frederik Erbs Spang Thomsen*

*   Fix `travel_to` to set usec 0 when `with_usec` is `false` and the given argument String or DateTime.

*   Add configurable deprecation warning for singular associations

    This adds a deprecation warning when using the plural name of a singular associations in `where`.
    It is possible to opt into the new more performant behavior with `config.active_record.allow_deprecated_singular_associations_name = false`

    *Adam Hess*

*   Fix `ActiveRecord::Store` to serialize as a regular Hash

    Previously it would serialize as an `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess`
    which is wasteful and cause problem with YAML safe_load.

    *Jean Boussier*

*   Add `timestamptz` as a time zone aware type for PostgreSQL
*   Fix previous change tracking for `ActiveRecord::Store` when using a column with JSON structured database type

    Before, the methods to access the changes made during the last save `#saved_change_to_key?`, `#saved_change_to_key`, and `#key_before_last_save` did not work if the store was defined as a `store_accessor` on a column with a JSON structured database type

    *Robert DiMartino*

*   Fully support `NULLS [NOT] DISTINCT` for PostgreSQL 15+ indexes.

content.content:
*   Add .md/.markdown as Markdown extensions and add a default `markdown:` renderer:

    ```ruby
    class Page
      def to_markdown
        body
      end
    end

    class PagesController < ActionController::Base
      def show
        @page = Page.find(params[:id])

        respond_to do |format|
          format.html
          format.md { render markdown: @page }
        end
      end
    end
    ```

    *DHH*

*   Add headers to engine routes inspection command
*   Add comprehensive support for HTTP Cache-Control request directives according to RFC 9111.

    Provides a `request.cache_control_directives` object that gives access to request cache directives:

    ```ruby
    # Boolean directives
    request.cache_control_directives.only_if_cached?  # => true/false
    request.cache_control_directives.no_cache?        # => true/false
    request.cache_control_directives.no_store?        # => true/false
    request.cache_control_directives.no_transform?    # => true/false

    # Value directives
    request.cache_control_directives.max_age          # => integer or nil
    request.cache_control_directives.max_stale        # => integer or nil (or true for valueless max-stale)
    request.cache_control_directives.min_fresh        # => integer or nil
    request.cache_control_directives.stale_if_error   # => integer or nil

    # Special helpers for max-stale
    request.cache_control_directives.max_stale?         # => true if max-stale present (with or without value)
    request.cache_control_directives.max_stale_unlimited? # => true only for valueless max-stale
    ```

    Example usage:

    ```ruby
    def show
      if request.cache_control_directives.only_if_cached?
        @article = Article.find_cached(params[:id])
        return head(:gateway_timeout) if @article.nil?
      else
        @article = Article.find(params[:id])
      end

      render :show
    end
    ```

    *egg528*

*   Add assert_in_body/assert_not_in_body as the simplest way to check if a piece of text is in the response body.

*   Add `config.action_dispatch.strict_freshness`.

    When set to `true`, the `ETag` header takes precedence over the `Last-Modified` header when both are present,
    as specified by RFC 7232, Section 6.

    Defaults to `false` to maintain compatibility with previous versions of Rails, but is enabled as part of
    Rails 8.0 defaults.

    *heka1024*

*   Support `immutable` directive in Cache-Control

def colorize_logging=(val)
        ActiveSupport::LogSubscriber.colorize_logging = val
        generators.colorize_logging = val
      end

      def secret_key_base
        @secret_key_base || begin
          self.secret_key_base = if ENV["SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY"]
            generate_local_secret
          else
            ENV["SECRET_KEY_BASE"] ||
              Rails.application.credentials.secret_key_base ||
              (Rails.env.local? && generate_local_secret)
          end
        end
      end

      def secret_key_base=(new_secret_key_base)
        if new_secret_key_base.nil? && Rails.env.local?
          @secret_key_base = generate_local_secret
        elsif new_secret_key_base.is_a?(String) && new_secret_key_base.present?
          @secret_key_base = new_secret_key_base
        elsif new_secret_key_base
          raise ArgumentError, "`secret_key_base` for #{Rails.env} environment must be a type of String`"
        else
        end

        def generate_local_secret
          key_file = root.join("tmp/local_secret.txt")

          unless File.exist?(key_file)
            random_key = SecureRandom.hex(64)
            FileUtils.mkdir_p(key_file.dirname)
            File.binwrite(key_file, random_key)
          end

          File.binread(key_file)
        end
    end
  end

content.content:
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "sidekiq/job"

module Sidekiq
  class Rails < ::Rails::Engine
    class Reloader
      def initialize(app = ::Rails.application)
        @app = app
      end

      def call
        @app.reloader.wrap do
          yield
        end
      end

      def inspect
        "#<Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader @app=#{@app.class.name}>"
      end
    end

    # By including the Options module, we allow AJs to directly control sidekiq features
    # via the *sidekiq_options* class method and, for instance, not use AJ's retry system.
    # AJ retries don't show up in the Sidekiq UI Retries tab, save any error data, can't be
    # manually retried, don't automatically die, etc.
    #
    #   class SomeJob < ActiveJob::Base
    #     queue_as :default
    #     sidekiq_options retry: 3, backtrace: 10
    #     def perform
    #     end
    #   end
    initializer "sidekiq.active_job_integration" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        include ::Sidekiq::Job::Options unless respond_to?(:sidekiq_options)
      end
    end

    config.before_configuration do
      dep = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("7.0", "Sidekiq")
      dep.deprecate_methods(Sidekiq.singleton_class,
        default_worker_options: :default_job_options,
        "default_worker_options=": :default_job_options=)
    end

    # This hook happens after all initializers are run, just before returning
    # from config/environment.rb back to sidekiq/cli.rb.
    #
    # None of this matters on the client-side, only within the Sidekiq process itself.
    config.after_initialize do
      Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
        config[:reloader] = Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader.new

        # This is the integration code necessary so that if a job uses `Rails.logger.info "Hello"`,
        # it will appear in the Sidekiq console with all of the job context.
        unless ::Rails.logger == config.logger || ::ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(::Rails.logger, $stdout)
          if ::Rails::VERSION::STRING < "7.1"
            ::Rails.logger.extend(::ActiveSupport::Logger.broadcast(config.logger))
          else
            ::Rails.logger.broadcast_to(config.logger)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

*   Allow signed ID verifiers to be configurable via `Rails.application.message_verifiers`

    Prior to this change, the primary way to configure signed ID verifiers was
    to set `signed_id_verifier` on each model class:

      ```ruby
      Post.signed_id_verifier = ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier.new(...)
      Comment.signed_id_verifier = ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier.new(...)
      ```

    And if the developer did not set `signed_id_verifier`, a verifier would be
    instantiated with a secret derived from `secret_key_base` and the following
    options:

      ```ruby
      { digest: "SHA256", serializer: JSON, url_safe: true }
      ```

    Thus it was cumbersome to rotate configuration for all verifiers.

    This change defines a new Rails config: [`config.active_record.use_legacy_signed_id_verifier`][].
    The default value is `:generate_and_verify`, which preserves the previous
    behavior. However, when set to `:verify`, signed ID verifiers will use
    configuration from `Rails.application.message_verifiers` (specifically,
    `Rails.application.message_verifiers["active_record/signed_id"]`) to
    generate and verify signed IDs, but will also verify signed IDs using the

# Rails 7.0.8.7 → 8.1.0: changes that affect Margin Notes

**Summary.** Two kinds of risk dominate. First, the app's own test suite would catch most problems, but about ten of them change behavior without raising an error in production:
- Import batches can now be partially saved.
- The import receipt loses its DOIs.
- Import previews lose their annotations.
- Digests cover the reader's local day instead of the UTC day.
- BigDecimal job arguments can't be read by an old worker during a deploy.

Second, several things only fail in Sidekiq jobs, after boot.

I compared the released gems for 7.0.8.7 against 8.1.0, read the changelogs of the latest patch in each series in between (7.1.5.2, 7.2.2.2, 8.0.3), and traced each relevant change into the app. The unpacked gems are in `/tmp/railsgems/<version>/<gem>/`. I didn't change, install, or run anything. The app tree is still clean.

Each claim is tagged **[changelog]**, **[code]** (gem or app source I read), or **[inference]**. Changelog links point to the stable-branch CHANGELOGs, e.g. `https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md`. The GitHub search API hit its rate limit, so the only PR I confirmed is #48600.

## Facts about the app that the ratings depend on

- **Defaults:** `config.load_defaults 7.0` (config/application.rb:12). The ratings assume you keep 7.0 defaults at first. Settings that only change when you raise `load_defaults` are listed under M4.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL through `pg` 1.6.0. MySQL, SQLite and Trilogy changes are ruled out.
- **Background jobs:** Active Job uses Rails' **built-in Sidekiq adapter** with Sidekiq 6.5.12 and redis 4.8.1 (application.rb:24). `ExportJob` is a native Sidekiq job. Tests use the `:test` adapter. Sidekiq 6.5 requires Rack 2, and Rails 8.1 still accepts Rack ≥ 2.2.4, so Rack stays on 2.2.
- **Rendering:** HTML only, with ERB, Sprockets, importmap and Turbo. There are no `.jbuilder` views or JSON endpoints.
- **Rich text:** Action Text with a vendored Trix 1.3.5 loaded as a classic script (layouts/application.html.erb:13). `@rails/actiontext` is pinned to `actiontext.js` (config/importmap.rb:8).
- **File storage:** Active Storage on the Disk service, with no `image_processing`.
- **Caching:**
  - Production has no `cache_store` set, so it uses the framework default, with `perform_caching` on.
  - There is one fragment cache, in exports/_export.html.erb:26.
- **Time zones:** Users store Active Support zone names (`users.time_zone`), and the app zone is UTC.
- **Secrets:** Provider settings come from `config/secrets.yml` through `Rails.application.secrets`.
- **Deprecations in production:** `report_deprecations = false`, so deprecation warnings are invisible in production.
- **Tests:** controller and model tests only. `test/system` is empty, so nothing checks behavior in the browser.
- **Ruby:** 3.3.6 (8.1 needs ≥ 3.2). The pins `concurrent-ruby 1.3.4` and `minitest ~> 5.25` satisfy 8.1's constraints. New dependencies include `action_text-trix`, `rackup`, `rack-session` and `useragent`.
- **Version choice:** 8.1.0 was released 2025-10-22. Later 8.1 releases exist (8.1.1 through 8.1.4), including the security releases 8.1.2.1 and 8.1.3.1. Consider targeting the latest 8.1 patch.

## High risk (behavior changes without an error)

**H1. An early `return` inside `transaction` now commits.**
- **Where:** app/models/import.rb:53-58 (`return false unless row.note.save` inside `transaction`).
- **Before:** 7.0 rolled back a block that exited early after writing. [code]
- **Now:** In 8.1, `within_new_transaction` commits unless an exception was raised or the thread is dying. The setting that controlled this was removed in 8.0. [code, changelog AR 7.1/7.2/8.0, PR #48600]
- **What breaks:** If a later row fails, the Import, the earlier notes and any new shared Citations stay saved. Meanwhile the preview tells the reader "Nothing has been saved", and resubmitting creates duplicates.
- **Tests:** imports_controller_test.rb:65-67 should fail. [inference]

**H2. `citation[:id]` returns nil.**
- **Where:** app/models/import.rb:68. The `citations` table's primary key is `doi`, and there is no `id` column (db/schema.rb:55).
- **Before:** `read_attribute(:id)` mapped to the primary key.
- **Now:** It is removed (deprecated 7.1, removed 7.2), and in 8.1 a missing attribute reads as nil without raising. [changelog, code]
- **What breaks:** The receipt CSV's DOI column comes out blank.
- **Tests:** imports_controller_test.rb:45 catches it.

**H3. `HashWithIndifferentAccess#stringify_keys` now converts Integer keys to strings.**
- **Where:**
  - `Import#annotations` keys the hash by Integer line number (import.rb:38-42).
  - imports/preview.html.erb:22 calls `stringify_keys`.
  - Line 42 looks entries up with `annotations[row.line]`, an Integer.
- **What breaks:** In 8.x every lookup misses, so annotations silently disappear from the preview. [changelog AS 8.0.0.rc1, code]
- **Tests:** imports_controller_test.rb:22,24,62 catch it.

**H4. Time-with-zone job arguments keep their own zone (7.1.3).**
- **Where:** `User#request_digest` passes `requested_at` in the reader's zone (user.rb:51,57). DigestMailer uses `requested_at.to_date` and `.all_day` (digest_mailer.rb:8-9).
- **Before:** The argument arrived in UTC, so the digest covered the same UTC day as the Redis reservation key (user.rb:52).
- **Now:** It covers the reader's local day. The subject date and the chosen notes change for anyone not on UTC. [changelog AJ 7.1.3, code: both serializers]
- **Tests:** digests_controller_test.rb:33-35 catches it.

**H5. BigDecimal job arguments are stored in a new format, which breaks a mixed deploy or a rollback.**
- **Where:** user.rb:57 passes a `BigDecimal`.
- **Before:** 7.0 passed it through as a primitive, and Sidekiq stored `"0.6667"`.
- **Now:** 8.1 always wraps it as `{"_aj_serialized":"ActiveJob::Serializers::BigDecimalSerializer",...}`. The opt-out setting was removed in 8.0. [changelog AJ 7.1/7.2/8.0, code]
- **Mixed versions:**
  - A 7.0 Sidekiq worker can't load that serializer. It raises `DeserializationError`, and `DigestJob` keeps retrying. [inference from the 7.0 source]
  - In the other direction, 8.1 reads old payloads fine, because the mailer calls `BigDecimal(string)`.
  - The new `time_zone` key from H4 is simply ignored by 7.0 workers.
- **Mitigation:** Upgrade or drain the workers before the web servers, and don't roll back while such jobs are queued. Alternatively, pass `completion.to_s`.

**H6. `TimeWithZone#to_time` now keeps the full zone.**
- **Where:** note.rb:44 `reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`, rendered at notes/_reminder.html.erb:19.
- **Before:** The result had a fixed offset, so after DST ended the preview showed "09:00 -04:00".
- **Now:** It shows "08:00 -05:00". That is the same instant, and the postponed reminder still uses `.to_i`, so stored data is unchanged. [changelog AS 8.0/8.1, code]
- **Impact:** This affects the display and ARCHITECTURE.md, and arguably fixes it.
- **Tests:** reminders_controller_test.rb:20-21 asserts the old value.

**H7. A negative cache `expires_in` is handled differently.**
- **Where:** exports/_export.html.erb:26 passes `export.expires_at - Time.current`, which is negative once an export has expired.
- **Before:** 7.0 wrote an entry that was already expired.
- **Now:** 8.1 drops the option, logs `ArgumentError` at error level, reports it to `Rails.error`, and caches the "Expired" fragment with no expiry. [code]
- **Impact:** The content stays correct, but you get error logs on every render.
- **If you adopt the 7.1 default** `raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time`, the exports page returns 500 whenever an expired export exists.

These three are also silent, but affect fewer users:

- **H8. Time zone mapping changed (7.2).** "Astana" moved from Asia/Dhaka to Asia/Almaty (current tzdata puts it at UTC+5, not UTC+6 [inference]). Readers who chose Astana will enter and see reminder times one hour off; the stored epochs don't change. "Greenland" and "Canberra" moved to equivalent zone IDs, and "Asuncion" was added. [code diff of `MAPPING`]
- **H9. Blob analysis now touches the records that own the attachment (Active Storage 7.1).** The chain is Blob → Attachment → `ActionText::RichText` (`touch: true`) → Note. So `Note#updated_at` moves to whenever `AnalyzeJob` runs. DigestMailer filters on `updated_at`, so a note saved near midnight UTC, or while workers are backed up, can move to the next day's digest. You can switch this off with `config.active_storage.touch_attachment_records = false`. [code; impact is inference]
- **H10. `to_plain_text` output changed.** Ordered-list numbering now counts only element siblings: imported HTML with whitespace between `<li>` items used to number 2., 4. and now numbers 1., 2. Text inside `<script>` and `<style>` is now dropped. This changes the Markdown export (export.rb:78) and the truncated previews. They are bug fixes, but the generated files differ. [code diff]

## Medium risk (errors where the fix needs a decision)

**M1. `Rails.application.secrets` was removed (7.2).**
- **Where:** citation/provider.rb:13 (a default argument) and config/secrets.yml. The tests also use it (citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:45,117-122).
- **Failure mode:** It isn't caught at boot. The `NoMethodError` is raised inside `CitationEnrichmentJob`, and it isn't a `Provider::Error`, so Sidekiq retries. The citation stays "Pending", and citation.rb:16 then answers "already being fetched" to every new request.
- **Decision:** credentials, ENV, or `config_for` (which keeps the same YAML-with-ERB shape). [changelog railties 7.1/7.2, code]

**M2. `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags` now defaults to nil (7.1).**
- **Where:** config/initializers/action_text.rb:3 does `nil + [...]`, which raises `NoMethodError` at boot.
- **Decision:** The defaults now live in `sanitizer_allowed_tags`. A naive `= %w[details summary]` would boot but silently strip attachments, `figure`, `figcaption` and everything else.
- **Fix:** Rebuild the list as `sanitizer.class.allowed_tags + [ActionText::Attachment.tag_name, "figure", "figcaption", "details", "summary"]`.
- **Caution:** If you later adopt the HTML5 `sanitizer_vendor`, the sanitizer is swapped in `after_initialize`, after your initializer has already run. [inference]
- **Tests:** notes_controller_test.rb:137 covers this. [changelog AT 7.1.0.beta1, code]

**M3. The built-in Sidekiq adapter is deprecated in 8.1 and goes away in 8.2.**
- **Status:** It works in 8.1.0 with Sidekiq 6.5.12, which already handles the 7.1 logger API. The warning won't show in production. [code]
- **Decision:** Moving to Sidekiq ≥ 7.3.3 brings redis-client, and these call sites would likely break [all inference, not checked against Sidekiq 7 source]:
  - `redis.sadd` returns 0 or 1 instead of a boolean (user.rb:38). Since 0 is truthy in Ruby, digests would be sent again for the same day.
  - `rescue Redis::BaseError` (notebook.rb:28) and the `Redis::CannotConnectError` tests would no longer match.
  - Strict arguments would reject `{ format: "markdown" }` (notebook.rb:26).

**M4. New defaults you'll face when raising `load_defaults`:**
- **7.1 `raise_on_assign_to_attr_readonly`:** The notebook form resubmits the slug (notebooks/_form.html.erb:13, notebooks_controller.rb:40), so every settings save would raise.
- **7.1 `default_column_serializer = nil`:** `serialize :preferences` (notebook.rb:7) would raise. Choose `coder: YAML` to keep reading the stored rows; picking JSON would break existing data.
- **7.1 `raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time`:** see H7.
- **7.2 `postgresql_adapter_decode_dates`:** `select_rows` would return `Date` objects, and `Date.iso8601(Date)` raises `TypeError` in the activity report (notebook.rb:40).
- **8.0 `strict_freshness`:** The ETag would win over Last-Modified in export_downloads_controller.rb:11.
- **Opt-in `enqueue_after_transaction_commit`:** Not on by default in 8.1. If you enable it, `Citation#request_enrichment` (citation.rb:15-22) and `Note#schedule_reminder` (note.rb:57-68) lose the "a failed enqueue rolls back" guarantee.

**M5. Trix and `actiontext.js`.**
- **What changed:** In 8.1, Action Text depends on Trix 2.1.15 through `action_text-trix`. Its `actiontext.js` is now a UMD bundle, and the ES module build moved to `actiontext.esm.js`. [changelog, code]
- **App setup:** The app imports the UMD file through importmap and loads Trix 1.3.5 itself.
- **Assessment:** It probably still registers the upload listener, but nothing checks that in a browser. [inference]
- **Decision:** Keep Trix 1.3.5 or move to Trix 2. The reason given in the layout comment for vendoring (the Trix 1.3.4 bug) no longer applies. Rails' Trix bump for CVE-2024-34341 doesn't help the vendored 1.3.5. [inference]

## Low risk (mechanical; boot or tests catch them)

- **note.rb:12** `serialize :tags, JSON` raises `ArgumentError` at class load. Use `coder: JSON`.
- **note.rb:10** `enum status: {...}, _prefix: true` raises `ArgumentError` (keyword form removed in 8.0). Use `enum :status, {...}, prefix: true`.
- **note.rb:14** `alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color` raises `ArgumentError`, because `color` is a store accessor. Use `alias_method` for the reader and writer.
- **notes_controller.rb:12** `where(notebooks: @notebook)` relied on plural names for singular associations, removed in 7.2. Rails now queries `"notes"."notebooks"`, which raises an SQL error. Use `notebook:`.
- **notes/index.html.erb:12** `form_with(model: nil, ...)` raises `ArgumentError`. Drop `model:`.
- **citation_enrichment_job.rb:7** `wait: :exponentially_longer` raises "Couldn't determine a delay" only when a retry happens, so the failure block never runs. Use `:polynomially_longer`, which is the same formula.
- **note.rb:61** `set(wait_until: <Integer>)` fails with `NoMethodError` on `utc` while the job is serialized. Pass `Time.at(epoch)`.
- **export.rb:42** `fragments.sum` over strings raises `TypeError` in ExportJob, leaving the export "working" while Sidekiq retries. Use `join`. This was already deprecated in 7.0.
- **test.rb:31** `show_exceptions = false` is now treated like `:all`, so the `assert_raises(RecordNotFound)` tests fail. Use `:none`.
- **Development secret:** it moved from `tmp/development_secret.txt` to `tmp/local_secret.txt`. Development sessions reset, and existing attachments in the development database stop resolving until you copy the file. [inference]
- **`has_secure_password`** now enforces a 72-byte maximum on passwords (7.1).
- **routes.rb:18** multi-path `get`: 8.0 deprecated it, and the 8.1.0 changelog says it was removed, but the 8.1.0 mapper still maps both paths without a warning. [code] Split it anyway.
- **schema.rb** will change on the next dump: columns sorted alphabetically (8.1) and `pg_catalog.plpgsql` (8.0).
- **notebook.rb:40** `Note.connection` is soft-deprecated, with no warning.

## Judged not relevant

- **Database adapters:** MySQL, SQLite and Trilogy changes. The app uses PostgreSQL.
- **Action Mailbox:** loaded by `rails/all`, but there's no ingress.
- **Action Cable:** there are no channels. The Redis adapter now needs `redis >= 4`, and 4.8.1 qualifies.
- **Cache stores:** Redis and Memcache store changes don't apply to the file, memory and null stores the app uses.
- **Active Storage:** variants, previews, S3/GCS/Azure services, and the Azure removal in 8.1 don't matter for the Disk service with no image processor.
- **JSON escaping defaults:** there are no JSON responses.
- **Generator-only additions:** Solid Queue, Cache and Cable, Kamal, the authentication generator, `allow_browser`, rate limiting and PWA files.
- **Unused Active Record features:** encryption, composite keys, sharding and multiple databases.
- **Removed queue adapters:** the Sucker Punch and Que removals.
- **Security headers:** CSP and Permissions-Policy are both commented out, and the Permissions-Policy middleware is now only added when configured.
- **Signed IDs:** the legacy verifier stays the default, so stored and bookmarked blob URLs keep verifying.
- **Rack 3 status renames:** Rack stays on 2.2.
